title: Write SEO content briefs that get cited in AI answers
summary: Build an answer-first content brief for a query: outline, questions to cover, evidence you still need, and a short quotable block. No fake stats and no guaranteed citations.

tests.prompt:
Write an SEO content brief meant to earn citations in search and AI answers — without guaranteeing placement.

Target query: [SEARCH QUERY]
My site / angle: [ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION]
Audience: [WHO]
Tone: [e.g. plain expert]
Approximate length: [WORD COUNT]
Must-cover facts I already verified: [BULLETS OR "none yet"]
Competitor / example URLs to learn from (optional): [1–5 URLs]

Produce a plain-text brief with:
1) User intent (what they actually want)
2) Answer-first outline (H2/H3) that leads with a direct answer
3) Questions to answer (People-also-ask style) — mark any you are unsure about
4) Evidence checklist: what sources or original data we still need
5) Quotable 40–60 word definition or answer block
6) Internal links / assets to include if we have them: [LIST OR blank]
7) What not to claim (hype, unverified stats)

Do not invent statistics or study results. If evidence is missing, list it under Evidence checklist.

setup.agent: Any chat model; optional Make/Zapier to turn a keyword sheet into brief drafts
steps: Pick one query and note what you can already prove.
Run the prompt and review the evidence checklist.
Gather missing sources before writing the article.
Write to the brief; keep the quotable block near the top.
Publish and monitor search Console / referrals over time — not overnight.
setup.approvalStep: A human removes any invented numbers before the brief goes to a writer.
failureModes: Promising AI citations as a guarantee

toolPicks.why: Keyword sheet → brief draft in Docs.
toolPicks.whenNot: You brief a few posts a month by hand.

toolPicks.why: Custom brief pipeline into your CMS.

faq.q: Does a good brief guarantee AI citations?
faq.a: No. It improves clarity and cite-ability. Ranking and citation systems still decide.

faq.q: How detailed should the brief be?
faq.a: Detailed enough that a writer who is new to the topic could draft without guessing facts.
